title: Mixtral of Experts
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. The report does not describe training-data sources, sizes, filtering, de-duplication, or quality control. The only data-related detail is that Mixtral was pretrained on multilingual data with a 32k-token context, and that the proportion of multilingual data was "significantly upsampled" relative to Mistral 7B, which the authors credit for strong French/German/Spanish/Italian results. The Pile validation set is used only for routing analysis, not for training.
curriculum: Training proceeds in two stages for the chat model. First, the sparse-MoE base Mixtral 8x7B is pretrained on multilingual data with a 32k context. Second, Mixtral 8x7B – Instruct is produced by supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on an instruction dataset followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on a paired feedback dataset. This is the standard pretrain → SFT → preference-optimization ordering; there is no RLHF/PPO loop, no multi-stage RL, and no self-play. The stated rationale is that SFT+DPO yields a chat model that beats GPT-3.5 Turbo, Claude-2.1, Gemini Pro, and Llama 2 70B-chat on human evaluation.
method: The core contribution is architectural: a decoder-only Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) transformer. Each of 32 layers replaces the FFN sub-block with 8 SwiGLU experts; a top-2 router G(x)=Softmax(TopK(x·Wg)) picks 2 experts per token and additively combines outputs: y=Σ Softmax(Top2(x·Wg))_i·SwiGLU_i(x). This gives 47B sparse / 13B active parameters. It resembles GShard but replaces all FFN blocks (vs every other) and uses simpler top-2 gating. Efficient inference uses Megablocks sparse-matrix kernels and Expert Parallelism. The post-training method for instruction following is SFT then DPO (Rafailov et al. 2023), which optimizes the policy directly from pairwise preferences without a separate reward model or PPO, the practical trick that yields Mixtral – Instruct.
eval_metrics: Evaluated with the authors' own pipeline: commonsense (HellaSwag, WinoGrande, PIQA, SIQA, OpenbookQA, ARC-E/C, CommonsenseQA), world knowledge (NQ, TriviaQA), reading (BoolQ, QuAC), math (GSM8K maj@8, MATH maj@4), code (HumanEval, MBPP pass@1), aggregates (MMLU 5-shot, BBH, AGIEval), plus multilingual French/German/Spanish/Italian, long-context passkey retrieval (100% accuracy) and proof-pile perplexity, and bias (BBQ, BOLD). Instruct models use MT-Bench and LMSys Arena Elo. Headline: Mixtral 8x7B matches/beats Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 (MMLU 70.6%, GSM8K 74.4% 8-shot, MATH 28.4%); Mixtral-Instruct scores 8.30 on MT-Bench and Arena Elo 1121, ahead of Claude-2.1 (1117), GPT-3.5-Turbo (1117), Gemini Pro (1111), Llama-2-70b-chat (1077).
key_results: Mixtral 8x7B (13B active / 47B sparse) matches or beats Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 with 5× fewer active params: MMLU 70.6%, GSM8K 74.4% (8-shot maj@8) vs Llama 2 70B's 69.6%, MATH 28.4% vs 13.8%. Mixtral 8x7B – Instruct reaches MT-Bench 8.30 and LMSys Arena Elo 1121, the best open-weights model as of Dec 2023, ahead of Claude-2.1 (1117), GPT-3.5-Turbo (1117), Gemini Pro (1111), and Llama-2-70b-chat (1077).
evolution_note: Mixtral builds on the GShard/Shazeer sparse-MoE line and the Mistral 7B architecture, and adopts DPO (2023) in place of PPO-based RLHF for instruction tuning. As one of the first open-weights sparse-MoE LLMs to match dense 70B quality at 5× lower active compute (Jan 2024), it validated open MoE as a cost-efficient path and motivated the wave of open MoE releases that followed.
